questions.questionText:
Consider the following Boolean expression where a and b are integer variables:

!((a > 10) || (b <= 5))

Which of the following expressions is logically equivalent to the expression above under De Morgan's Laws?
questions.explanation: Applying De Morgan's Law for a negated OR expression, !(A || B) becomes !A && !B. Inverting each relational sub-expression: !(a > 10) simplifies to (a <= 10), and !(b <= 5) simplifies to (b > 5). Combining them with logical AND yields (a <= 10) && (b > 5).

options: Compilation error due to missing parentheses around logical operators
Cannot be determined without knowing the value of p
questions.explanation: Following Java operator precedence: (1) Parentheses: (q || r) is (false || false) = false. (2) Unary NOT (!): !p is !true = false; !(false) = true. The expression becomes: false || q && r || true. (3) Logical AND (&&): q && r is false && false = false. The expression becomes: false || false || true. (4) Logical OR (||): false || false is false; false || true is true. Thus, the expression evaluates to true.

questions.questionText:
A student wants to execute a block of code only when the integer variable age is between 13 and 19, inclusive. The student writes the following condition:

!(age < 13 || age > 19)

Which of the following is logically equivalent to the student's condition?
questions.explanation: Under De Morgan's Law, !(A || B) is equivalent to !A && !B. Here, !(age < 13) becomes age >= 13, and !(age > 19) becomes age <= 19. Combining with && produces age >= 13 && age <= 19, representing the inclusive range [13, 19].
